items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: I think in Stanley Dance's book he mentions that you said that King Oliver was having problems, too.

ctx.x: No, he didn't go on to New York with us. That's when he -- he had lip trouble and he had to have it pierced and he knew only about one doctor in St. Louis that could do the job. And after he had it pierced, then he couldn't play for quite a while till it healed properly.
I think in Stanley Dance's book he mentions that you said that King Oliver was having problems, too.

Well, King Oliver, he had pyorrhea real bad, and in those days, I mean, they didn't treat pyorrhea like they do now, you know. A lot of times the poor man was suffering so bad he couldn't even blow his horn and his teeth would hit the roof of his mouth half of the time, they were so weak.
